title: The Russia–Ukraine war
summary: From Crimea in 2014 to today's front line, and why Europe, grain and gas prices care.

stops.caption: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the largest war in Europe since the Second World War.
In 2014 Russia annexed Crimea, a move most UN members do not recognise, and fighting began in the eastern Donbas region.
Russian forces advanced on the capital, Kyiv, in 2022 but withdrew from the north after weeks of fighting.
Fighting runs along a front of about 1,000 km in the east and south; drones and missiles strike far beyond it.
Ukraine exports huge amounts of grain through Black Sea ports, so the war has moved world food and energy prices.
European countries cut Russian gas imports, sent aid to Ukraine and raised defence spending. Finland and Sweden joined NATO.
